## Intent

Make the second-attempt rule mechanical. Any relaunch, replacement worker, or validation run past its third fix round must refuse to start another implementation attempt until a Sol spec pass exists for this task. The gate must be enforced mechanically from existing control-plane actions: fm-control relaunch of a ship or scout that already had an implementation attempt, a replacement worker for the same existing task, and a no-mistakes validation run entering its third fix round. On those triggers refuse another implementation worker until a Sol spec artifact exists for the task under data/<id>/report.md or the scout-plus-promote-owned spec path, naming the missing spec and directing the operator to commission the Sol spec scout without guessing a model. First implementation attempts and --secondmate launches remain unaffected, as does non-replacement recovery. Constraints are withheld capabilities, not prose. Do not implement Sol model picking, staged Sol on first dispatch, or brief-scaffold-h1. Reuse scout plus promote, with no new control plane, daemon, or wrapper. Keep refusal mechanics in owning script headers and portable executable behavior tests in tests/. The current PR also needs the pre-existing intermittent fm-watcher-lock stopped-watcher SIGCONT-to-SIGTERM race fixed through a deterministic resume barrier before TERM, with regression coverage and focused serial validation. Do not add agent names as commit co-authors. Preserve the existing PR 17 and branch custody, never merge, force, reset, rebase, stash, amend, replace the branch, drop parents, or discard work. Validate with the acceptance scenarios: first fm-spawn succeeds without a Sol spec; relaunch without a spec refuses and writes no replacement agent; the same relaunch proceeds once the Sol report/spec exists; replacement spawn without a spec refuses; --secondmate is unaffected; and the watcher-lock serial regression passes. Do not hand-edit around an active no-mistakes run; drive all gates through no-mistakes responses.

## What Changed

- New `bin/fm-second-attempt-lib.sh` mechanically refuses a second implementation worker for a ship task until `data/<id>/spec.md` exists: it is wired into `fm-control.sh relaunch` (before the running agent is stopped) and `fm-spawn.sh --relaunch`, triggering on a durable `spawn_gen=` record or on a `state/<id>.nm-third-fix-round` marker it writes when the branch-and-head-attributed no-mistakes status reports an active fix round of 3 or later. Unreadable markers refuse rather than guess; scouts, secondmates, and first attempts stay ungated, and teardown removes the marker with the rest of task state.
- The recovery path reuses the existing scout+promote flow: `fm-brief.sh --scout --sol-spec` scaffolds a spec-writing scout whose deliverable is `data/<id>/spec.md`, and `fm-promote.sh <scout-id> --sol-spec-for <gated-ship-id>` installs that reviewed artifact at the gated task's own spec path under both lifecycle locks, refusing an uncommissioned source, an empty or differing spec, or an ungated target, and leaving the gated task's worktree, branch, PR, and meta untouched. New `bin/fm-scout-artifact-lib.sh` owns the declared-artifact contract via `data/<id>/.deliverable` and is consumed by teardown's work-product gate, `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` readiness/`scout_reports[]`, and `fm-captain-hold.sh` origin proof.
- Fixed the intermittent stopped-watcher SIGCONT-to-SIGTERM race in `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh` by adding a bounded barrier on a fresh heartbeat before sending TERM, registered `fm-second-attempt.test.sh` in the serial family in `fm-test-run.sh`, and added executable coverage across second-attempt gating, brief scaffolding, task delivery, teardown, captain-hold lifecycle, and fleet-snapshot views, with matching updates to `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The two fixes in this round are narrow, fail-closed, correct against the real emitted no-mistakes label format and the existing declared-artifact classifier, and are covered by behavioral tests that would fail if the code were wrong; the only issue found is an incomplete sentence in a secondary doc.

## Testing

<code>I ran the change-relevant behavior suites (fm-second-attempt, fm-watcher-lock, fm-brief, fm-captain-hold-lifecycle, fm-fleet-snapshot-view, fm-task-delivery, fm-teardown, fm-control, fm-control-relaunch) and they all pass. For product-level evidence I drove the real fm-spawn, fm-control and fm-promote executables through the intent&#39;s acceptance scenarios and captured the operator terminal transcript: a first ship spawn succeeds with no Sol spec anywhere, a relaunch refuses while leaving the running agent alive and sending no lifecycle input, the same relaunch proceeds once data/&lt;id&gt;/spec.md exists, a replacement fm-spawn --relaunch refuses, a secondmate relaunch is exempt (it reaches the later agent-free check, proving the gate ran and let it through), and a fixture no-mistakes status reporting `auto-fix 3/9` writes state/&lt;id&gt;.nm-third-fix-round=3 and refuses by naming fix round 3. The transcript also shows the documented recovery clearing the gate in place and an ordinary scout&#39;s undeclared stray spec.md being refused for install. For the watcher-lock race I ran the full suite three consecutive times green and measured the barrier&#39;s resume window at a consistent ~5.0s, which is the interval the pre-fix code sent SIGTERM into; I could not make the pre-fix case fail locally (0 failures in 14 runs including under heavy CPU load), so that measurement rather than a before/after failure is the evidence that the race window was real. This change is CLI-facing with no rendered UI surface, so the terminal transcripts are the end-user artifact. The worktree is clean and all scratch fixtures were removed.</code>
